journal_entries.text: Acquired a bill of landing at Nexus Prime. Cost 250 credits for the privilege of docking and trading. Officer Larsen warned about unarmed travel through dangerous systems.
Delivered Odom's iron ore to the Main Foundry intake at Forgeworks.
Met Elena Reeves at the Nexus Prime cantina, at a table facing the departure boards.
Earned trade access at Breakstone by delivering food to the miners' commissary. Hanna Voss ran the docks.
Met Marcus Jin at Breakstone. Mining foreman, twenty years on station. He said his team flagged the air recyclers on the Nexus Prime orbital, and the report came back deferred.
Met Dr. Priya Osei at Nexus Prime. Her chartered transport to Axiom Labs had been reassigned, and her research samples were time-sensitive.
Met Tomas Drifter at Haven's Rest. Accepted a gray-market trade: rerouting supplies past Guild tariffs.
Met Tomas Drifter at Haven's Rest. Declined his offer to reroute supplies around Guild tariffs.
Responded to a distress signal from a freighter under pirate attack. Met Captain Reva Sato, Guild military escort. Three convoy attacks this month, same pattern.
Passed a freighter sending a distress signal. Later heard Captain Reva Sato arrived too late. Three convoy attacks this month.
Glyn Quintela, information broker, approached at the Nexus Prime cantina. Offered intel on the pirate attacks in exchange for a delivery to Crimson Reach. No questions asked.
Delivered a package to Malia Torres at Crimson Reach. She said whoever was backing the pirates had serious resources.
Attended faction summit at Axiom Labs. All four factions present. No agreement reached. Guild wants military response, Union wants solidarity, Collective wants data, Alliance wants independence.
Ambushed by pirates during travel. Survived the attack. Their ships were well-equipped.
Found Oren Tak in Breakstone's mining tunnels. Retired miner. Came away with a location: Iron Depths, Sublevel 7.
Located a pirate command base near Iron Depths. Scan data showed an active operations center.
Presented evidence of the pirate base to faction leaders. Chose an ally for the operation ahead.

The pirate operation is funded by a rogue faction within the Commerce Guild. They call themselves The Ledger. Goal: destabilize shipping, monopolize security, control the Expanse. Base neutralized. Leaders escaped.
The Ledger was exposed but not destroyed. Uncharted coordinates recovered from the base pointed to more operations beyond the Expanse's borders. The factions were talking.
Odom filed a freight violation against my permit over his iron ore. Guild standing dropped. His desk was closed to me after that.

What Arna told me about running hot. Three legality tiers: legal moves anywhere; restricted needs papers (faction permits, customs stamps, full manifest trail); illegal is contraband (weapons, narcotics, biohazards, stolen goods). Penalties escalate: warn, fine, confiscate, ban. Each faction enforces differently. Every system has an inspection rate tied to its enforcement. Heat builds when you run dirty and decays when you do not. Smuggling compartments installed at shipyards hide contraband from routine checks (persistent searches still find it). Black markets are hidden behind rep or introductions. She taught me all of this while bleeding through a compress.

Arna's younger brother was on a Union refinery station. His lungs were giving out from processed air. Union healthcare gave him two options: keep working or pay out of pocket for transfer. The transfer cost more than she made in ten years. She said the ore, the refining, the sale, the ambush, all of it was for him.

Went back to Heron's Mark. Keren was waiting. The depot held more than the sale was worth. Arna was packing a bag. Two blacklists instead of one. She said something small and walked off toward the dock.
Clean pull at a derelict in Haven's Rest. Nothing followed us out. Arna stayed behind at the manifest desk the whole time.
I turned Arna in. She didn't look at me. I didn't look at her either. I got paid. The docks kept running.

Said goodbye to Arna at the departure bay. She had a duffel bag at her feet. Not much else. She told me about the pendant before she went: it was her mother's. She said she wanted one thing she'd said to me to be true. Then she walked toward the freighter bound for Port Kestrel and she did not look back.

Naveen Prakash confirmed what the restricted sector's maintenance logs imply: the DCMC reclassification does not match any standard hazard assessment. Someone cleared the records using a document form he has only seen once before, in a review that was sealed weeks after he submitted his findings. He has filed four supplementary notes. None of them have been read.

Yuki Tanaka flagged an anomaly at Nova Research. A deep-field reconnaissance signal was routed directly to the restricted wing, bypassing the shared logging repository. Her discrepancy report was acknowledged, then the acknowledgment's own access log was stripped. Someone in that wing has clearance that does not appear on any org chart she can access.
Turned in my first contract at the Wreckers' Guild Hall. Malia weighed the haul, logged it, paid me out. No ceremony.

Journeyman now. Malia signed off on it without making a thing of it. Recovery pulls open up. Higher-margin work, higher exposure. She said journeyman is when the Guild starts trusting you with the bigger pieces.

Master tier at the Guild Hall. Malia stopped calling me kid. She did not say so, just stopped. Deep-derelict work is on the board now. Old hulls, bad orientations, partial atmosphere. The kind of pulls that need a name on them.

Squared the missed contract with Malia. She did not lecture. She just opened the board back up and said the Guild forgets a debt once. Then she handed me a torch and asked me to hold the line on the next one.

Funded my first project at the Okafor Institute. Kweon walked me through the board, named the failure rate on every line, and said the principle is unchanged even when the application has to adapt. The capital is committed. The trial decides.

First project resolved. The trial held. Kweon said the methodology survived contact with the data and the result is publishable in its current form. The patent is filed in my name; the disposition is mine. She added that she does not say it often enough that she is grateful.

First failed project at the Institute. Kweon delivered the debrief in the same register she delivers the successes. The methodology was sound; the result was not what the modeling predicted. Resources were not allocated for a second cycle this quarter. The variance data is in the file. A portion of the capital came back. The rest is the cost of the answer.
First patent moved off held. The disposition went on file. Either the patent stayed in circulation under license, or the lump sum went into the account.

Sten Brygaard told the story the way he tells it. Cargo Bay 7. Third shift, morning cycle. Sora Takahashi climbed up on a shipping crate. She was short. Everyone forgets how short she was, he said. She told the bay: we built this, all of it, and we are done letting other people decide what it is worth. That was the speech. Sten said it twice, the second time for me to hear it.

Sten said: nineteen days. He did not say it was a strike. He said it was nineteen days of people not coming up out of the shafts. He said: they did it worker by worker. Nobody made a list of heroes. The list would have been the whole roster. The Charter signed because the bays were quiet for nineteen days, not because of one speech.

Sten poured a second cup. He said: the Breakstone Charter, 2267. The signing was in this bay. Sora signed first because she happened to be standing closest to the table. He says she would have hated being the symbol. He says she got over it.

Sten said the collapse came forty years after the Charter. Section 6 went down on a third shift. Fourteen people. We got eleven names on that wall, he said. Three were never recovered. He pointed at the wall. He did not read the names out. He said: every shift change, somebody puts their hand on it. That is the rotation.

Sten said: Marcus Jin's father was at the walkout. Stayed the full nineteen days. So was a thousand other people, he said. Marcus knows what the Union owes him and what it does not. He said the work continues. He said: come back when you are out this way again. The flowers refresh on a rotation.

Odom cracked open the part of the ledger most pilots never saw. Talked about putting credits to work in places that paid back over time. There were stations in the Expanse that ran structured returns on parked capital.

First session at the Verdant council. Three delegates and a mayor, three different ideas of what the bill was about. The vote went the way it went. Hask anchored the soil. Drift carried the data. Marsh held the water number. Vance kept the floor moving.
Got the concession out before the vote. The bill failed on the floor. The delegate I worked in mediation came out of the session with a position that shifted two steps.
Had the count before the session opened. Two pre-commits in the corridor, one of them quiet. The bill passed.

First session at the Alliance Congress in Haven's Rest. Four delegates and four different reads on the same resolution. Wentworth tracked precedent. Shirane drafted the deal. Vasc held the principle. Tejada spoke for the Reach. The room ran slower than Verdant and the stakes scaled across settlements.
Had a delegate locked before the session and watched the pre-commit break mid-arc. The room saw it. The vote went sideways for a round. I rebuilt what I could and walked out with something.

Carried a Congress vote that rippled beyond Haven's Rest. Markets at two settlements moved on the resolution. Built a coalition that held in two settlements at once. Bigger room. Slower clock. The vote stood.

First session at the Guild arbitration floor. Malia ran it like a transaction: no drama, just position and record. The delegates came in knowing what they wanted. Two of them had been in the same room before. The vote resolved.

Got the concession before the vote closed. The floor did not hold, but the work in the corridor moved one delegate enough to take it off the record. Malia wrote it neutral. The Guild field rights stayed unchanged. What shifted was the delegate's position on the next case.
Ran the mediation myself. Malia stepped back and recorded. The position I had to hold was not the one I argued for. The session closed on a win. Malia said nothing at the end.
First session. Lot prices moved differently than on the commodity floor. The ceiling was whatever the room would pay. Sable said two words the whole time.
Won my first lot. Took it at the price the room held. Filed the receipt.
A name showed up on the floor. They bid against me for a lot. Lost that one.
Talked to the auctioneer between sessions. Cassian Velo. Off the floor he was quieter.
First session at the Reach Floor. The crates came in off a flatbed and the Floor Manager called the lots in three sentences. There are no records here. The reserve is the reserve.
Met the Floor Manager. Vex Tarn. He runs the floor. He does not run a conversation. He told me how the floor opens and what he does not take returns on. That was the meeting.
Won a lot the Stellaris Commerce Guild would not have signed off on. Two points off the standing ledger. Vex did not comment. The crate was already on the trolley.

Filed my first consignment at the Stellaris floor. Paid the listing fee at the desk. The fee was the floor's whether the lot moved or not. The crate went onto the catalogue under a number, not my name.
Sold my first lot from the seller side. Hammer landed above the reserve. Velo read the price and the catalogue moved on. Credits cleared into the account by the time I left the floor.
Reserve was not met. The lot went back to my hold. The fee stayed with the floor. The room had its limit and I had set mine, and the two did not meet.

The project that came out of the Institute this cycle was clinical work. Pediatric methodology, field clinic logistics, something that goes toward patients instead of a balance sheet. Kweon said: this is what the building was for. She said it once, and then the conversation moved on.

First project out of the Institute on the commercial side. Propulsion efficiency or industrial analysis, one of the ones that pays well and publishes in sector trade journals. Kweon said: the Institute's accounting does not separate concern from yield. Both pay for the same bench time. She did not say she approved.

Kweon sat me down and named the pattern. Heal-aligned completions running well ahead of the rest across a long run of funding. She said: you funded work that would not have happened otherwise. That matters. She said it directly, which is not how she usually talks. The pediatric data is published. The field clinic supply chain is in the archive. The vaccine synthesis holds.

Kweon named what the funding history looked like from her side. Commercial and industrial outcomes running ahead of clinical work over a long run. She said: the pediatric cohort study sat unfunded for two cycles. The field clinic work was deferred once. That is the cost.

The countersignature work held up. Aldric Senn was on the paperwork and not on the map. The file on him closed today, not the way it started. The map above him is still there to be walked. Priya offered the referrals. I said yes.
The file on Aldric Senn closed today. He and the leadership who fled with him were the only witnesses left who could have said why the home galaxy was chosen. That question went unanswered.

Chose the ledger. Cradlepoint charter is off the roster. Castellano opened the leverage line and the discreet-buyer list. Kallio's people will run the concourse racks without my ships. The money that used to flow that way is earning against Coinmark now.

Chose the concourse. Coinmark line stopped at cash in hand from today. Kallio opened the Cradlepoint dock channels and put me on the guaranteed-demand contracts. The leverage window is gone. What I can pick up at Haven's Rest, I carry.

Chose the pursuit. Odusanya's circuit was closed to me after that. The warrant-holding line was gone. Rendik Foss and Callan Vert were still on the open board. The people who could help reach them did not ask about jurisdiction.

Chose the warrant. Odusanya filed the civilian warrant-holding authorization. It is on record now. Rendik Foss and Callan Vert are still at large. The bounty board has them. I made the call anyway. The case-building contacts across the settlements are open to me because I did.

Chose the council seat. Owusu drafted it, the fourth-day quorum passed it, and it was mine. Deng's cells started running debt buyouts around this ship, and Halvorsen's registry did not read my signature. The council calendar did.

Chose the cells. Deng put the coordination across three settlements through this ship. Debt buyouts, safety comms, legal writs on the shift-supervisor writeups. Owusu would not seat me at the fourth-day quorum. Halvorsen would not file for me.

Chose the parcel. Halvorsen signed the administrator-of-record filing at Crimson Reach Claims and the border ground went on the registry as mine. Owusu would not seat me. Deng organized around this ship specifically. Surveyors on Halvorsen's circuit started routing drift reports to my office.

Chose the Institute. Solheim filed the wing dedication and the standing authority on the same day. My name went on the Farrow Institute's thirty-year endowment record. The crew kept doing what crews do when the captain is somewhere else.

Chose the crew. The Institute filed the wing without my name on it. I was at the table for the shift transition. Marcus asked Elena about her sister. Priya finished her readings at the console instead of her bunk. The roster is different now. I was there when it changed.

Chose the archive. Virtanen filed the standing authority the same week. The Long Yard was on the regional record, the boundary documented, the catalogue recognized. The sites I did not claim went to someone else. Halvorsen filed adjacent territory. I watched the development schedule fill in from outside the boundary.

Chose the claim. Halvorsen filed the producing-claim designation within a cycle. The territory generates yield. Virtanen relocated what he could save of the Long Yard to outside the boundary and kept working. The catalogue is smaller now. The sites inside the perimeter are on the development schedule. Both things are in the registry.

Chose the chapel. Solano filed the dawn-rotation invitation the same week and the Cradlepoint network acknowledged it without ceremony. The access was informal, which was how it worked there. Marchetti filed the procedure authorization on another applicant. I was not in that record.

Chose the procedure. Marchetti filed the authorization within a cycle on the basis of the ethics committee's review. The research materials are accessible now. Solano's rotation continued without me on the roster. The chapel is still open three mornings a week. I am not on the list. Both things are on the record.

Chose the Understair. Wulan Doyle filed the standing access the same week, no per-run negotiation required. The Kettlebridge brokers put the ship inside the ledger. Kallio's dock channels at Cradlepoint closed. The list at Haven's Rest kept its rotation without this name on the manifest.

Chose the community side. Kallio has the docks open and a list of families that needs to be shorter. The Understair account is closed. Wulan Doyle's floor operations continue at Stellaris Port without this ship on the access list. The ledger on her side does not include this route anymore. What can be picked up at Haven's Rest, gets carried.
Kimura signed for what was on the scale, received short. The incident report covered the rest.
Made up Odom's count after a fight took ore from his load. Kimura weighed ten. Odom wrote the difference on my side of his book.
Odom wrote off his iron ore: ten units, one hundred fifty credits. He called it the once.
Handed Odom's iron ore job back. His dock crew took the ore off the ship. Nothing was owed either way.
Odom paid the iron run on the count. His screen showed the floor log for his ore beside Kimura's count.
Told Elena Reeves to mind her own business. Left her table at the Nexus Prime cantina.
Turned down Glyn Quintela's chip run to Crimson Reach. He said he would be at the same table, third stool from the left.
